# Scrib SU -- 2026-09-01

Scheduled 10:00 CDT (15:00 UTC); the recording runs 00:00:24 to 00:43:11, so
about 43 minutes. The transcript carries relative offsets only, so the wall-clock
span comes from the calendar slot, not from the file. All nine listed attendees
spoke. Rajeev Kumar joined as new Bounteous-side project
manager and introduced himself at the start of the call.

## Summary

Rob introduced Rajeev Kumar as the new project manager on the Bounteous side,
covering PM and backlog upkeep rather than hands-on build work. Rob gave his
own update: flows re-rendered on the iOS emulator and exported to the Lucid
board, a mermaid diagram of backend calls generated from the prototype, and a
plan to build a meta-repo section documenting every screen, its features, and
backend calls, then turn that into the backlog.

Team status went around: Pramod confirmed GitHub access is sorted (Bounteous
is maintainer) and flagged that iOS builds will need a paid plan once build
minutes run out; Eric agreed to set that up. Pankaj is validating architecture
decisions and scaffolding an iOS build/TestFlight setup locally, and still
owes moving his Bitbucket PR to GitHub (holding off until backend repo
structure is settled). Nitish compared his schema draft against the POC
schema and prepared questions. Karuna is standing up a test management tool
(referred to as the "QV tool" in the transcript) and can create
test plans/cases and import cases generated via Claude, pending a VM. Shubhankar
is reviewing Pankaj's pushed code and docs, has cloud access, but is still
waiting on machine-level (Mac) access and GitHub approval.

The bulk of the call was Nitish's and Pankaj's backlog of product questions,
worked through live with Rob and Eric: repo structure for a hosted pages site
(privacy policy, invite pages), age/birth-date capture at signup, multi-channel
sharing and per-channel reaction tracking, stroke-data-based image compositing,
invite link expiry, moderation model, wall size/load expectations, and
multi-tenant/SSO auth needs. Several items were explicitly deferred to
tomorrow's standup (repo structure decision, Cognito vs. alternatives for
multi-tenant auth, mandatory-story-vs-skip decision, save-and-resume-drawing
decision).

## Questions / decisions

### Decisions

- Birth date will be captured at signup for all users, with no differentiation in app behavior between minors and adults for now (owner: Rob Forshier II / Eric Rice).
- A picture shared to multiple walls becomes a separate copy per wall; reactions/emojis on one wall's copy do not cross over to another wall's copy (owner: Rob Forshier II, confirmed by Eric Rice).
- Users can choose which walls (personal, family, etc.) a drawing gets added to; a drawing does not have to go to the personal wall if the user doesn't want it there (owner: Rob Forshier II).
- Posted images cannot be edited after posting; only the underlying stroke data is retained so composite images can be rendered without a flattened white background (owner: Rob Forshier II).
- No pre-publish moderation delay for now; posting is immediate, with moderation deferred and possibly crowdsourced (reports/downvotes) added later if needed (owner: Rob Forshier II, agreed by Eric Rice).
- Invite links should not expire, to avoid the re-invite loop seen in the prior version (owner: Eric Rice).
- Multi-tenant/SSO support (e.g. enterprise B2B crossover) is a later-phase concern, not part of the first build (owner: Rob Forshier II).
- At minimum, a drawing must be posted to the user's personal wall; it cannot be created and kept off every wall (owner: Rob Forshier II). This sits in tension with the pick-and-choose decision above. Rob said both, earlier that a user "might not want to throw it in your personal wall" and later that "at the bare minimum, they can just put it in just their personal." Treat the personal-wall rule as unsettled and confirm it.
- Standard field-level validation (e.g. valid email format at signup) is expected (owner: Rob Forshier II).

### Questions

- Do we host the privacy-policy/invite pages as a separate repo or a folder in a monorepo? (raised by Pankaj Aggarwal, deferred to 2026-09-02)
- When the same image draws reactions across multiple walls, do we track reactions per wall or aggregate them, and does the user get a cumulative personal view across walls? (raised by Nitish Goyal and Pankaj Aggarwal; Eric Rice's answer: keep reactions separate per wall, but a nice-to-have would be a cumulative personal-archive view)
- What is the expected load per wall (number of images, e.g. a 500-person public wall via QR code) and should the UI plan for virtual scrolling or filtering? (raised by Pankaj Aggarwal, not fully resolved)
- Is a story mandatory when posting a drawing, or can it be skipped? (raised by Karuna Arshakota, answer deferred to 2026-09-02)
- Can a user save a half-finished drawing and resume later, or is the app meant to be a single spontaneous session (the "Wordle" comparison raised by Matthew Kaplan)? (raised by Eric Rice and Pankaj Aggarwal, answer deferred to 2026-09-02)
- Should auth use Cognito, or does multi-tenant/per-tenant control require an alternative? (raised by Pankaj Aggarwal, deferred to 2026-09-02)
